newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish parliament to consider PM censure bid.
newsitem.headline: Turkish parliament to consider PM censure bid.

text.p: Parliament will debate today whether to take up an opposition censure motion against Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan in the first challenge to his rule since he became modern Turkey's first Islamist leader in June.
"The debate will be at 1500 (1200 GMT)," a parliamentary spokesman said.
But it looks unlikely the opposition will succeed in toppling the prime minster.

MPs will debate Erbakan's bid to redirect foreign policy towards Turkey's Arab and Moslem neighbours, a move that has drawn fire from the secular opposition, elements of the armed forces and Ankara's close patron Washington.

That effort blew up in the prime minister's face 10 days ago when Libyan leader Muammer Gaddafi used an Erbakan visit as a platform to blast Turkey's ties to the West and its treatment of its Kurdish minority.
Erbakan's stunned silence in the face of these remarks, as well as his own anti-Western rhetoric while in Libya, provoked condemnation at home and a broadside from the U.S. state department.
However, the three main opposition factions, who agree on little but the desire to remove Erbakan, are likely to come up short in their bid to topple the prime minister.

On paper the opposition needs 276 votes, a majority of the 550 seats, to guarantee victory. It can count on up to 269 MPs from its own ranks, plus a handful of dissidents from Erbakan's coalition ally, the conservative True Path Party led by Foreign Minister Tansu Ciller.
The iron discipline of Erbakan's Islam-based Welfare Party all but bars defections.
